reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, resource-level rubric, fresh-review framework, Basic resource-review context, full Basic StructureDefinition report material, deterministic aggregate, local R4/R6 Basic StructureDefinitions, Basic terminology artifacts, R4 maturity map, and behavior reports for direct `Basic` references. No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding named Basic; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: Basic is trial-use/FMM 1 in R4, so the compatibility burden is weak compared with mature or normative resources. That lowers the case for reopening proportionate cleanup, but it does not erase the need to map the mandatory modifier `Basic.code` safely where Basic is actually used.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Basic keeps its identity and local model; no resource-level migration program is unavoidable, but `Basic.code` needs deliberate terminology migration guidance.

reasoning.thesisMd: Basic remains the same non-abstract DomainResource specialization with the same canonical URL, resource type, local element set, element names, cardinalities, summary flags, and modifier structure. There are no local R4-to-R6 hard instance breaks. The only forward compatibility concern is that mandatory modifier `Basic.code` changes from an example binding to the R4 Basic Resource Types value set to an extensible binding to version-independent resource type codes.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is mostly stable with one local conformance/semantic chore. Existing R4 `Basic.created` date values remain acceptable at date precision in R6 `dateTime`, and all R4 `Basic.author` target types remain allowed after R6 adds `Device` and `CareTeam`. R4 instances that used lower-case or abbreviated `basic-resource-type` codings may need terminology mapping or dual-coding policy, but the resource is not removed, remodeled, or made invalid by local element shape changes.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a broad Basic migration program is not already unavoidable, avoidable compatibility problems should still be judged per change. The value of preserving compatibility is highest for `Basic.code` because it is mandatory and a modifier; the reverse-only `created` precision and `author` target expansions are local mixed-version/downgrade concerns rather than reasons to accept unrelated future breaks.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: For `Basic.code`, lower-cost mitigation is more compelling as migration guidance than as a full base-model rollback: publish a ConceptMap or explicit dual-coding guidance from `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/basic-resource-type` to R6 current/old resource type codes. Keeping the old example binding or adding the old code system to the R6 extensible value set would preserve more old-only codings, but it risks duplicate representations on a modifier element and weakens the R6 cleanup toward version-independent resource identifiers. No less-breaking base design is needed for `created` or `author` in the R4-to-R6 direction because both are widenings for old content.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The behavior reports contain no direct finding with `affectedResources` including `Basic`. The 11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings, including Resource-level operation removals and shared search-parameter metadata changes, can affect generic FHIR infrastructure that serves Basic, but they are not Basic-specific resource model evidence and do not change the Basic migration conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: This independent review agrees with the deterministic aggregate's headline: major migration `No`, migration shape `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks`, and compatibility posture `preserve-compatibility-per-change`. The aggregate's high structure-impact count is mostly reverse-version pressure from `created` and `author`; the resource-level conclusion should be driven instead by the absence of hard forward structural breaks and the single meaningful forward `Basic.code` terminology concern.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The main uncertainty is terminology and usage evidence for `Basic.code`: the supplied files do not include an official R4-to-R6 ConceptMap, terminology-server expansion/applicability analysis, or production Basic usage data. That uncertainty affects how much mapping work real implementations face, not the conclusion that Basic is not broadly remodeled.

findingConsiderations.title: Basic.code binding changed from example Basic Resource Types to extensible version-independent resource types
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `Basic.code` is mandatory and remains a modifier that determines what kind of Basic resource is being represented. R6 changes the binding strength and value set, so old-only R4 `basic-resource-type` codings can create terminology warnings, local errors, or dispatch/mapping work. This is the only forward-facing Basic-local issue substantial enough to keep the resource from `low-material-change`; it warrants targeted terminology migration guidance, but not a resource-level migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Basic.created widened from date to dateTime
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a widening for R4-to-R6 because R4 date precision remains valid in R6 `dateTime`. It matters for reverse conversion, generated model types, storage precision, and mixed-version equality/order logic when R6 systems use timestamps, but it does not make existing R4 Basic instances invalid or drive a forward migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: Basic.author added Device and CareTeam reference targets
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R6 adds `Device` and `CareTeam` while retaining every R4 `Basic.author` target. That is additive for R4-to-R6 validation. Implementations downgrading R6 content or using exhaustive target-type switches need policy for the new targets, but this is a local reverse/mixed-version chore rather than a forward compatibility break.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared Resource-level operation removal is important for generic servers and clients, including those that expose Basic endpoints, but it is not a Basic-specific behavior finding and should be handled in the Resource/API migration track rather than counted as Basic model redesign.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The shared search-parameter metadata change can affect generated clients and conformance tooling for all resources, but Basic is not Resource or DomainResource itself. It remains infrastructure context and does not alter the Basic resource-level conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or confirm `Basic.code` migration guidance, ideally a ConceptMap or explicit dual-coding recommendation from R4 `basic-resource-type` codes to R6 version-independent resource type codes where a resource-type concept applies.

For implementations, inventory Basic instances that use only the R4 Basic Resource Types code system and decide whether to map, dual-code, or retain local codings with documented extensible-binding rationale.

Treat `Basic.created` timestamp precision and new `Basic.author` target types as R6-to-R4 or mixed-version policy items; they should not be used as evidence that all R4 Basic instances require forward transformation.

caveats: The inspected R6 package is 6.0.0-ballot4; final R6 publication material could alter or explain these deltas.
No official Basic R4-to-R6 diff, Jira rationale, terminology expansion, or ConceptMap was supplied for `Basic.code`.
No direct behavior finding named Basic; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered context only under the review rules.
No production usage corpus was supplied, so prevalence of old Basic Resource Types codings is uncertain.
